bullets.title: NVDA: Citi raises Jul/Oct-Q estimates; $300 PT maintained ahead of Aug 26 earnings
bullets.body: Citi raises NVDA Jul-Q revenue estimate to $93B vs Street $92B and Oct-Q to $105B vs Street $103.7B, lifting F27-29 EPS 1-2-2%. B300 ramp continues, HBM supply secured through 2026-27, and Vera Rubin units revised to 2M. Separately, China approved small batches of H200 chips for ByteDance and Tencent (~10k units each). Citi also flags the Aug 21 $4.2T options expiry and notes NVDA's 16% pre-earnings rally is the largest since May 2025; historical data shows -2.8% average on earnings day. SMH Nov-26 $600 calls recommended as preferred vehicle.

bullets.title: KEYS: Multiple upgrades, PT raised to $400-$425 on record AI wireline orders
bullets.body: Keysight beat F3Q26 consensus across the board—revenue $1.85B vs $1.77-1.80B preview, orders $2.09B (record, +52% y/y organic), gross margin +510 bps y/y to 69.0%. F4Q guide of $1.93-1.95B (+37% y/y) at high end of expectations. Goldman upgrades to Buy ($452 PT), Morgan Stanley raises PT to $425 (OW), JPM raises PT to $425, Citi raises PT to $400 (Buy). AI test intensity broadening across 800G/1.6T and silicon photonics; supply is primary growth constraint. FY26 EPS raised ~12-13% across the Street.

bullets.title: AVGO: Citi previews F3Q with $116B F27 AI revenue; MediaTek competition risk flagged
bullets.body: Citi maintains Buy on AVGO with $500 PT (19x F28E EPS). Jul-Q modeled slightly above consensus at $29.4B; Oct-Q modeled below on ~80 bps gross margin compression as AI ASIC mix rises to 44%. F27 AI revenue held at $116B, above AVGO's prior $100B target but below the $130B market expectation, with downward pressure from data center readiness delays and permitting challenges. MediaTek raised its AI ASIC market share target to 15-20% (~$18B by 2027), creating share-loss risk.

bullets.title: SNOW: Mizuho's top pick into earnings; PT raised to $355; BofA reinstates Buy ($130 PT)
bullets.body: Mizuho raises SNOW PT to $355 (from $295), citing data modernization as meaningful growth driver and expects another product revenue beat (~34% YoY per Morgan Stanley). Cortex Code in ~33% of active deals; competitive coexistence with Databricks by workload. BofA reinstates Buy with $130 PT. Separately, SNOW is rolling out dynamic model routing. Stock up 80-85% since late May earnings, making setup more difficult but fundamentals still constructive.

bullets.title: CRWD: High Q2 expectations after 115% YTD run; net new ARR bogey $310-315M vs Street $285M
bullets.body: JPMorgan flags CRWD as facing an unusually high bar heading into Q2 results (reports Aug 26). Investors expect net new ARR of $310-315M vs Street $285M—a near 100 bps sequential acceleration required. Q3 ARR guidance must show further acceleration to ~$340M vs Street $330M. Mizuho also raises CRWD PT to $240 (from $175) on positive cybersecurity checks. Stock up 115% since April's Mythos launch.

bullets.title: RDDT: ChatGPT citation share collapsed 86% to 0.5% after Aug 8; licensing risk resurfaces
bullets.body: JPMorgan's Tech Sketch flags Reddit citations in ChatGPT search results fell from 3.8% share to 0.5% (86% drop) after August 8th, raising questions about the value of Reddit's content licensing agreement with OpenAI. Pre-market RDDT -1.5%. Separately, DUOL inadvertently disclosed 27.4% DAU growth on Aug 17 (vs. 23% in Q2), driving DUOL +8.6% pre-market.

bullets.title: NBIS: $4.5B convertible notes offering; Pennsylvania data center order is moderately negative
bullets.body: Nebius announced a $4.5B convertible senior notes offering in two tranches ($2.75B due 2030, $1.75B due 2034) to fund data center construction, GPU procurement, and full-stack AI cloud development. Separately, Pennsylvania Governor Shapiro's executive order restricting data center development is viewed as a direct but 'moderately negative' and 'not thesis-breaking' development for NBIS's Pennsylvania project. Pre-market NBIS -3.5% (grouped with CRWV -3.5%, IREN -2.4%).

bullets.title: TLN/VST/CEG: Pennsylvania data center executive order hits IPPs; limited impact on well-capitalized developers
bullets.body: PA Governor Shapiro signed an executive order removing all data center projects from the fast-track permitting program, requiring GRID standards (energy affordability, environmental, workforce) and local approvals. TLN fell 11% as the largest PA gas generator (5.3 GW). Goldman and Morgan Stanley see limited impact on well-capitalized developers but speculative projects bear the burden. Constellation Energy (CEG) cited as clearest beneficiary given the Crane/Three Mile Island project. GE Vernova expanding local PA factory.

bullets.title: INTU: Piper bearish; FY27 initial guide likely below consensus, investor apathy expected until F3Q27
bullets.body: Piper's morning call flags multiple INTU headwinds: FY27 initial guidance likely below consensus, Desktop and Mailchimp growth talked down, TurboTax pricing changes creating uncertainty. Analyst expects investor apathy to persist until F3Q27. INTU reports Aug 25 after close (consensus EPS $3.54, revenue $4.28B).

bullets.title: LOW: EPS beat but comps miss and FY26 guidance cut to lower bound; stock -3.3% pre-market
bullets.body: Lowe's Q2 EPS $4.40 beat consensus $4.22 (incl. $0.11 tariff refund), but comps +0.2% missed +0.5% estimate. FY26 guidance lowered to $92B revenue (from $94B range) and EPS ~$12.25 at the low end of prior range, with flat comps vs prior flat-to-+2%. DIY discretionary remains weak vs. Pro/online strength. Gross margin contracted ~80 bps to 33.0%. UBS maintains Buy ($285 PT), Citi maintains Buy ($267 PT), KeyBanc maintains Overweight ($275 PT). Multiple analysts note widening gap vs. Home Depot.

bullets.title: TJX: 2Q beat on comps and EPS; Marmaxx +1% miss could pressure multiple; FY27 guidance raised
bullets.body: TJX Q2 comps +4% beat Street +3.3%; EPS $1.22 beat $1.19E. HomeGoods +10%, TJX International +11%, Canada +6%, but Marmaxx +1% vs. +2% expected. FY27 EPS guidance raised to $5.15-5.20 from $5.08-5.15. Q3 EPS guidance $1.30-1.32 is below Street's $1.35. UBS maintains Buy; Citi flags valuation re-rating needed (27-30x) for meaningful upside, sees ROST risk at domestic division. Long-term store target raised by 500 to 7,500.

bullets.title: META: $1.4T youth liability trial begins; Mizuho sees headline risk but manageable
bullets.body: 29 state AGs filed suit seeking up to $1.4T in damages plus injunctive relief requiring platform redesign. Day 1 featured internal emails showing Instagram's 'overall company goal' was 'teen time spent.' Trial expected 6-8 weeks. Mizuho maintains Outperform ($750 PT), arguing minors are not significant monetization sources and social media has First Amendment protections unlike tobacco. Hedgeye flags broader talent/culture risk as key long-term threat.

bullets.title: AAPL: EU ATT prompt changes likely to boost opt-in rates; App Store EU fee cuts unlock mobile app upside
bullets.body: Apple agreed to modify ATT prompt in EU—removing 'track' language and changing buttons to 'Allow/Reject'—which should nudge opt-in rates higher in EU with limited US impact per JPMorgan. Separately, Apple is lowering EU app fees to 26% base (20% direct, 15% link-out) effective Oct 1. Morgan Stanley estimates 1-5% EBITDA uplift for most mobile internet names; RBLX among top beneficiaries at ~5.3% max uplift.

bullets.title: CIEN: Northland upgrades to Outperform, raises PT to $500 from $450
bullets.body: Northland Capital Markets upgrades Ciena to Outperform from Market Perform and raises price target to $500 from $450, implying ~23% upside from $405.54. Analyst is Tim Savageaux. FactSet consensus target is $583.19.

bullets.title: AAOI/LITE/MTSI: Optical supply demand imbalances flagged as 'extreme'; capacity booked through 2027
bullets.body: Multiple earnings prints (LITE, MTSI, AAOI) show extreme demand imbalances in lasers, TIAs, and DSPs; optical supply remains far behind AI-driven demand. AAOI management confirmed capacity is 'sold out at least through second half of next year and beyond' at the Rosenblatt conference. Separately, the silicon photonics production ramp is accelerating at leading foundries per KEYS commentary.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Talent exodus flagged as structural risk; AI search vs. See's Candies analogy
bullets.body: SemiAnalysis flags that all co-authors of 'Attention Is All You Need' have now left Google, including Jeff Dean departing for Discovery Loop, Noam Shazeer joining OpenAI, John Jumper at Anthropic. Cultural issues cited as headwinds. Ben Thompson draws an analogy comparing Google Search to Berkshire's See's Candies (high-margin cash generator) with AI investment as the railroad bet. Social media debate notes Google faces talent disadvantage vs. space/search/AI-native peers.

bullets.title: BABA: Earnings Thursday Aug 20 pre-market; JPM hosting post-results call Friday
bullets.body: BABA reports Q2 FY2026 (Thursday Aug 20 before open) with consensus EPS CNY10.14 and revenue CNY268.48B. Morgan Stanley recently upgraded BABA to OW citing MaaS scenario with 76% GPM and 53% op margin at 2.5-year payback. JPM hosting post-results conference call Friday Aug 21 at 4pm HK (no replay available). Analyst Alex Yao presenting.

bullets.title: Hedgeye Risk Range signals: AAPL flipped Bullish; ORCL, META, GOOGL, TSLA bearish
bullets.body: Hedgeye's Aug 19 Risk Range Signals flip AAPL from Neutral to Bullish and remove ORCL from active tracking (OutBucket, now Bearish). MSFT, AMZN, NFLX, NVDA, SNDK remain Bullish. META, GOOGL, TSLA assigned Bearish trend. Broad index signals remain Bullish (SPX 7,652-7,811, COMPQ 26,104-26,899). VIX and USD Bearish; Oil Bullish.

bullets.title: GS hedge fund flows: TMT most net bought; AI exposure rising but below May highs; de-grossing fading
bullets.body: Goldman Prime reports US equities net bought for 3 straight weeks—largest 3-week buying since March 2020 as % of market. TMT most net bought US sector MTD led by hyperscalers and semis. Broad AI exposure rose in August but remains well below May highs. Hedge fund net selling of AI Winners -1.8 std, hardware -3.0 std, memory -1.6 std in the Tuesday selloff—90% long reduction. Short exposure in US Macro Products at lowest YTD levels; option skews and GS Vol Panic Index declined sharply.

bullets.title: SNDK: Elevated options flow; memory upcycle intact as Vera Rubin drives TLC NAND demand
bullets.body: SNDK options flow was 'super active' on Aug 18 per unusual flow trackers. Memory upcycle context: Samsung is mass-producing 16TB PM1763 enterprise SSDs for Nvidia Vera Rubin; TLC spot prices rebounding. Morgan Stanley flags DDR4 prices may jump 50% in Q3 as chipmakers shift capacity to HBM. SNDK assigned Bullish trend by Hedgeye. MU noted as unable to meet more than half of customer demand.
